content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"Yes: it resolves a pressed-link collision between the parties' chains, the situation K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' — reading A: the judge weighs the whole chain's footing; reading B: the judge requires an explicit verse naming the channel.","why":"The judge makes the absence of an explicit naming verse decisive, rather than weighing the defender's and challenger's chains by footing."}
